questions.question: He asked her, "Where do you live?" (Change to Indirect Speech)
options: He asked her where she lives.
He asked her where she lived.
He asked her where did she live.
He asked her where she was living.

questions.question: "Is there anyone there?" he asked. (Change to Indirect Speech)
options: He asked if there is anyone there.
He asked whether there was anyone there.
He asked that there was anyone there.
He asked whether there were anyone there.

questions.question: The taxi driver asked me, "Where do you want to go?" (Change to Indirect Speech)
options: The taxi driver asked me where I want to go.
The taxi driver asked me where did I want to go.
The taxi driver asked me where I wanted to go.
The taxi driver asked me where I was wanting to go.

questions.question: She exclaimed, "How beautiful the rainbow is!" (Change to Indirect Speech)
options: She exclaimed that the rainbow is very beautiful.
She exclaimed with joy that the rainbow was very beautiful.
She exclaimed how beautiful the rainbow is.
She exclaimed with joy that the rainbow is beautiful.

questions.question: I asked him, "What is your name?" (Change to Indirect Speech)
options: I asked him what is your name.
I asked him what his name was.
I asked him what was his name.
I asked him what his name is.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence (Preposition with emphasis):
options: Gandhiji laid emphasis at non-violence.
Gandhiji laid emphasis on non-violence.
Gandhiji laid emphasis about non-violence.
Gandhiji laid emphasis in non-violence.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence (Passive with shocked):
options: Babuli was shocked by the dispute in her family.
Babuli was shocked at the dispute in her family.
Babuli was shocked on the dispute in her family.
Babuli was shocked with the dispute in her family.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence (Comparative Degree):
options: American Negroes are more richer than their brethren in Britain.
American Negroes are richer than their brethren in Britain.
American Negroes are the richest than their brethren in Britain.
American Negroes are most richer than their brethren in Britain.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence (It is time structure):
options: It is time we eat our food.
It is time we ate our food.
It is time we will eat our food.
It is time we have eaten our food.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence (Perfect Participle):
options: Having took our rest, we continued our journey.
Having taken our rest, we continued our journey.
Having take our rest, we continued our journey.
Having taking our rest, we continued our journey.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence (First Conditional):
options: If you get proper training, you will become successful.
If you will get proper training, you become successful.
If you got proper training, you would become successful.
If you get proper training, you would become successful.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence (Inversion with Hardly):
options: Hardly had he arrived when the train left.
Hardly he had arrived than the train left.
Hardly had he arrived than the train left.
Hardly he arrived when the train left.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence (Inversion with No sooner):
options: No sooner did he arrive than the meeting started.
No sooner did he arrive when the meeting started.
No sooner he arrived than the meeting started.
No sooner had he arrived when the meeting started.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence (Negative adverb hardly):
options: It hardly matters whether he says yes or no.
It hardly does not matter whether he says yes or no.
It hardly matter whether he says yes or no.
It hardly matters not whether he says yes or no.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence (Past time marker):
options: He celebrated his birthday yesterday.
He celebrates his birthday yesterday.
He has celebrated his birthday yesterday.
He was celebrating his birthday yesterday.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence (Infinitive of purpose):
options: The teacher told him to come late.
The teacher told him coming late.
The teacher told him come late.
The teacher told him that he comes late.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence (Gerund after deny):
options: The boy denied obeying the teacher.
The boy denied to obey the teacher.
The boy denied obey the teacher.
The boy denied that he obeys the teacher.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence (Past Simple V2):
options: He sent an email yesterday.
He sends an email yesterday.
He has sent an email yesterday.
He was sending an email yesterday.

questions.question: Identify the sentence in the Present Perfect Tense:
options: They have finished their work.
They has finished their work.
They are finishing their work.
They finished their work.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence (since + time):
options: It has been raining since morning.
It is raining since morning.
It has rained since morning.
It was raining since morning.
